1. The Government of the Republic of Marshall Islands has applied for financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the RMI Urban Resilience Project (RMIURP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. This assignment is intended to strengthen the technical and operational capacity of the Building Safety and Regulations (BSR) Division of the Ministry of Public Works, Infrastructure and Utility (MPWIU), in implementing the National Building Code (NBC) and the National Building Code Act. Through the engagement of a multidisciplinary firm, the assignment will provide specialized technical advisory services to support the implementation of the building regulatory system, improve regulatory processes, and enhance the technical capabilities of BSR staff. The assignment will also include targeted technical training for key stakeholders and the development of standard, code-compliant residential building plans to promote safe, affordable, and resilient housing. The complete scope of services, including the consultant qualification requirements, is indicated in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment, which can be obtained from the contact details provided below.

The Consulting Firm shall provide qualified experts across relevant disciplines over a period of eighteen (18) months to support the Building Safety and Resilience (BSR) Division in achieving the objectives of this assignment by implementing the following three activities under two components.

PART A (Time-Based)

Activity 1. Technical Advisory Services

PART B (Lump Sum)

Activity 2. Standard Residential Housing Plans

Activity 3. Training and Capacity Building

3. The BSR Division of the MPWIU now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

4. The attention of interested Consultants (Individuals) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

5. The best qualified firm to carry out the services will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Regulations and based on the following criteria:

  • The consulting firm shall have a minimum of ten (10) years of demonstrated experience in building code implementation, regulatory support, and/or building regulatory reform in developing country contexts. This shall include experience in: building code development, review, interpretation, or application; building design review and code compliance; relevant international standards (ICC, NFPA, ASCE, ASHRAE); building permit review processes; supporting construction inspection systems; and working within regulatory or compliance environments.
  • The Firm shall demonstrate relevant experience in providing building code implementation support, technical advisory services to building control authorities, institutional and capacity building for regulatory agencies, and/or the development of building regulatory systems, operational procedures, guidelines, or tools. Experience in low- and middle-income countries.
  • Prior experience working in the relevant region or in countries with similar construction practices, hazard profiles, and institutional contexts, especially small island developing states, will be considered an advantage.
  • The firm shall demonstrate experience in delivering training programs for government officials and professionals in the construction sector.
  • Experience working on World Bank-financed projects or other multilateral development bank projects is highly desirable.

(Prorogation de la date d'ouverture des plis du 21 juillet 2026 au 31 juillet 2026)

Travaux d’aménagements et de bitumage d’environ 10 km de voiries urbaines reliant les RN1, RN7 et RN8 (rocade) dans la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso

Référence de l’AOI :

Emis le 

 

03 juin 2026

1. Le Gouvernement du Burkina Faso a obtenu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour financer le coût du Projet de Mobilité et de Développement Urbain des Villes Secondaires (PMDUVS) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements prévus au titre du marché relatif aux travaux d’aménagements et de bitumage d’environ 10 km de voiries urbaines reliant les RN1, RN7 et RN8 (rocade) dans la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso. Pour ce marché, l’Emprunteur devra utiliser pour les paiements la méthode de décaissement intitulée « Paiement Direct », telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour les Financements de Projets d’Investissements.

2. Le Projet de Mobilité et de Développement Urbain des Villes Secondaires (PMDUVS) a pour objectif de développement d’améliorer la mobilité urbaine, l'accès aux services de base et aux opportunités économiques, et renforcer les capacités institutionnelles de gestion urbaine dans des villes secondaires sélectionnées au Burkina Faso. Afin d’atteindre cet objectif de développement, cet avis est publié dans le but de sélectionner une entreprise pour la réalisation des travaux d’aménagements et de bitumage d’environ 10 km de voiries urbaines reliant les RN1, RN7 et RN8 (rocade) dans la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso.

3.  L’Agence des Travaux d’Infrastructures du Burkina, agissant en qualité de Maître d’Ouvrage Délégué (MOD) pour la mise en œuvre dudit projet, sollicite pour le compte du Projet de Mobilité et de Développement Urbain des Villes Secondaires, des offres sous plis fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour exécuter les travaux d’aménagements et de bitumage d’environ 10 km de voiries urbaines reliant les RN1, RN7 et RN8 (rocade) dans la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso constitué d’un lot Unique.

Les travaux consistent essentiellement en l’installation du chantier, aux travaux préparatoires et des terrassements, à la construction :

  • d’une chaussée de 2 x (2 voies de 7,00 m de large) séparées par un terre-plein central (TPC) ;
  • TPC large de 46,00 m du pk 0+000 au pk 2+280, de 2,50 m du pk 2+300 au pk 10+900 y compris la bretelle de la rue 20.26 et de 0,60 m en DBA du pk 10+940 au pk 11+670 ;
  • de pistes cyclables de 2,50 m du pk 0+000 au pk 10+900 y compris la bretelle de la rue 20.26, de 2,00 m du pk 10+940 au pk 11+670 de part et d’autre de la chaussée ;
  • des arrêts de bus du pk 0+000 au pk 8+880
  • des trottoirs en pavé de largeur minimale 1,50 m du pk 0+000 au pk 11+670 ;
  • des caniveaux couverts en béton armé de sections différentes du pk 0+000 au pk 11+670 ;

Les profils en travers type sont définis dans le dossier des plans.

La structure de chaussée prévue consiste en la réalisation d’une couche de fondation de 20 cm d’épaisseur en graveleux latéritique amélioré au ciment sur la section allant du pk 8+880 au pk 10+100 et d’une couche de fondation de 21 cm d’épaisseur en graveleux latéritique amélioré au ciment sur le reste du tronçon, d’une couche de base de 10 cm d’épaisseur en grave bitume GB3, le revêtement de la chaussée en béton bitumineux à module élevé (BBME) de 5 cm d’épaisseur,  la piste cyclable est revêtue en béton bitumineux semi grenus (BBSG 0/6) et les trottoirs en pavé de 6 cm d’épaisseur.

Une couche de roulement de 18 cm d’épaisseur en béton armé de ciment BC4 constitue une structure de chaussée pour le cas particulier de la voie passant devant le Port-sec de Bobo-Dioulasso (pk 8+880 au pk 10+100 - Zone ZAD et Port Sec).

Le projet prévoit également la construction d’ouvrages d’assainissement et de drainage, la mise en place de la signalisation, de la vidéo surveillance et des dispositifs de sécurité routière, la mise en œuvre de mesures compensatrices environnementales et de sauvegarde sociale y compris les Violences Basées sur le Genre, les Exploitation, Abus Sexuel et Harcèlement sexuel.

Pour plus d’améliorations, il est prévu de l’éclairage public à travers des candélabres complètes à énergie solaire sur tout le long du projet.

Les aménagements à réaliser sont définis de manière détaillée dans le dossier des Plans.

Le délai d’exécution des travaux est estimé à dix-huit (18) mois y compris la saison pluvieuse.

4. La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence internationale en utilisant un Dossier d’Appel d’Offres tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation de Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteur de FPI » version 2016, révisé en septembre 2025 (« le Règlement de Passation de Marchés »), et ouvert à tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans le Règlement de Passation de Marchés.

5. Les Offres seront évaluées conformément au processus d'évaluation défini dans le dossier d'appel d'offres. Les pondérations suivantes s'appliqueront aux Critères notés (y compris les facteurs techniques et autres que le prix) : cinquante pour cent (50 %) et pour le coût de l'Offre : cinquante pour cent (50 %).

6. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations à l’adresse ci-dessous et examiner le Dossier d’Appel d’Offres tous les jours ouvrables aux horaires ci-après : le matin de 7 heures 30 minutes à 12 heures 30 minutes et l’après-midi de 13 heures à 16 heures.

7. Le Dossier d’Appel d’offres en français peut être acheté par tout Soumissionnaire éligible intéressé en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse ci-dessous contre un paiement de cent mille (100.000) francs CFA, correspondant au prix de vente du dossier. La méthode de paiement se fera par dépôt direct du montant d’achat du dossier sur le compte bancaire n° 01001 00100053312-10 ouvert au nom de Agetib à BSIC-Burkina. Le retrait du dossier se fera auprès de la Direction des marchés de l’Agetib sur présentation de la quittance de versement du montant d’achat du DAO.

8. Les soumissions doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 31 juillet 2026 à 10 h00 TU. La remise des soumissions (L’appel d’offres) par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Toute Soumission reçue en retard sera écartée.  Les enveloppes extérieures de l’Offre marquées « ORIGINAL DE L’OFFRE », et les enveloppes intérieures marquées « PARTIE TECHNIQUE » seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne qui souhaitent assister à l’ouverture des plis à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous le 31 juillet 2026 à 10 h 00 mn TU. Toutes les enveloppes marquées « PARTIE FINANCIÈRE » demeureront non-ouvertes et seront conservées dans un lieu sûr par le Maître d’Ouvrage jusqu’à la seconde ouverture publique des Offres.

9. Les Soumissions doivent être accompagnées (i) d’une Garantie d’offre, pour un montant de deux cent cinquante millions (250 000 000) F CFA, (ii) d’une Déclaration relative à l’Exploitation et aux Abus Sexuels (EAS) et/ou au Harcèlement Sexuel (HS), et (iii) d’une Déclaration d’Engagement de la main d’œuvre locale.

Les exigences en matière de qualifications figurant à la section III du DAO sont résumées dans le tableau suivant :

10.           AVIS A MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET N°003/2026

 

Nom du Projet : PROJET D’AMELIORATION DES RESULTATS D’APPRENTISSAGE DE L’EDUCATION DE BASE (PARAEB)

 

Intitulé de l’activité : recrutement d’une agence de communication pour la conception d’un microprogramme audio et visuel (images/illustrations) sur les exploitations, abus et harcèlement sexuel ET REALISATIONS DU PARAEB.

 

Don IDA Numéro : E-180

Identification du Projet : P175803

 

Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad a reçu un Don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour le financement du PARAEB.

L’Unité de Coordination et de Gestion du Projet invite les Agences de communication admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-après : la conception et l’impression des outils de sensibilisation sur les EAS/HS en milieu scolaire, du travail et de la communauté afin de contribuer à la sensibilisation des travailleurs/ouvriers, des élèves, enseignants, des leaders communautaires et religieux et les autres membres de la communauté sur les bonnes pratiques. Spécifiquement, il s’agit de :

  • La conception d’un scénario permettant de faire le montage audio et visuel et en 3D animé du microprogramme ;
  • La conception des illustrations positives sur les EAS/HS/VCE pour la diffusion ;
  • L’impression des boites à images, dépliants, affiches, brochures et kakemono sur la base des illustrations conçues et des messages clés élaborés par le Projet ;
  • La diffusion du microprogramme audio et visuel dans les radios communautaires, sur le site web du PARAEB et sur les réseaux sociaux ;
  • Le monitoring de la diffusion du microprogramme ;
  • La réalisation d’une banque des images, des dépliants, des affiches, des brochures et kakemono sur la base des réalisations globales du Projet.
  • Etc.

Les critères d’évaluation des dossiers sont mentionnés ci-après :

  • Dossier administratif conforme et en cours de validité ;
  • Preuves des réalisations similaires au cours des cinq (5) dernières années, de 2021 à 2025 (Elaboration des outils de sensibilisation, communication, publicité et marketing, élaboration des chartes graphiques, etc.) ;
  • Membres du personnel clé, affecté pour la mission et leurs CV et copies de diplômes.

Les manifestations d’intérêt écrites doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous en personne, par courrier, ou par courrier électronique au plus tard le 22 juillet 2026 à 11h 00 (heure locale) :

Par ailleurs, elles doivent être adressées sous pli fermé à M. le Coordonnateur National du PARAEB, Chef de Projet, avec la mention : « Manifestation d’intérêt relative à la sélection d’une Agence de communication pour les activités VBG du PARAEB et ses réalisations ».

procnotices.notice_text:
AVIS D’APPEL PUBLIC A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

Titre de la mission : Recrutement d’un partenaire facilitateur pour appuyer le Projet STAR RDC dans la réalisation des activités des Travaux à Haute Intensité de Main d’œuvre (THIMO) dans les Provinces du Kwango, Kwilu et Mai-Ndombe.

Date de publication                                : 14 juillet 2026

Date de clôture                                       :  04 août 2026

Lieu d’intervention                               :  Provinces de Kwango, Kwilu et Mai-Ndombe.

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Démocratique du Congo a sollicité et obtenu un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA)  d’un montant équivalent à US$ 250 millions de dollars en vue de financer le coût du Projet de Stabilisation et de Relèvement de l'Est de la RDC (« le projet » ou « STAR-Est » et se propose d’utiliser une partie les fonds de ce crédit pour financer les services suivants : soutenir la stabilisation et le relèvement par (i) la fourniture d'infrastructures socio-économiques communautaires de base à petite échelle ; (ii) la réinsertion socio-économique des personnes associées aux groupes armés dans leurs communautés dans les zones ciblées des provinces de Ituri, du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu et (iii) le renforcement des administrations provinciales.

 

2. Le présent   avis d’appel public à manifestation d’intérêt fait suite à l’Avis général de Passations des Marchés publié sur UNDB le 05 février 2024 et paru dans le journal « Médiacongo.net » du 12 février 2024 (Réf. MCN : AOF37491) - https://www.mediacongo.net/appel-societe-37491_star_est_avis_general_de_passation_des_marches.html.

 

3. Les services comprennent les services techniques d’appui au Projet STAR RDC dans la réalisation des activités des Travaux à Haute Intensité de Main d’œuvre (THIMO) dans les Provinces du Kwango, Kwilu et Mai-Ndombe.  Les Termes de Reference (TDR) de la mission peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous :dpm@star-rdc.org  avec copie à : recrutementstarest@yahoo.com; aayumbi_yumbiali@yahoo.com

 

4. Le Projet STAR RDC invite les candidats intéressés à présenter leurs candidatures en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent produire les informations sur leur capacité et expérience démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations. Profil requis pour la présélection :

  • Le PF THIMO doit être une agence de développement ou un bureau d’ingénieurs conseils, ayant des expériences prouvées dans la maitrise d’ouvrage déléguée (MOD) ou l’assistance à la maitrise d’ouvrage (AMO) ou dans le contrôle des travaux de projets d’infrastructures et ayant au moins 15 ans d’exercices ;
  • Il doit avoir mis en œuvre (MOD, AMO ou Contrôle de travaux) au moins cinq (5) projets de construction/réhabilitation de routes dont deux (2) projets de construction/réhabilitation avec approche HIMO de routes dans les pays à climat similaire (équatorial) en Afrique Centrale. Il doit aussi justifier en qualité de MOD ou AMO ou Mission de contrôle de travaux, la réalisation d’au moins trois (3) projets de construction de route mécanisées ou semi-mécanisée avec utilisation des engins lourds ;

Note : Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à ce stade de la présélection.

 

5. Les candidats peuvent s’associer pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives et augmenter leur chance de qualification mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l'association est sous la forme d'un groupement ou de sous-traitant. Dans le cas d'un groupement, tous les membres sont conjointement et solidairement responsables pour tout le contrat, en cas de sélection.

6. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions de la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI) (juillet 2016, révisée en Novembre 2017, Aout 2018, Novembre 2020, Septembre 2023, février 2025 et Septembre 2025) « Règlements de Passation des marchés »), relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts sont applicables.

7. Un consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode Sélection Basée sur la Qualité et Cout (QBSC). Les critères d’éligibilité, l’établissement de la liste restreinte et la procédure de sélection seront conformes aux « Règlements de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI) ((juillet 2016, révisée en Novembre 2017, Aout 2018, Novembre 2020 et Septembre 2023 et février 2025) « Règlements de Passation des marchés » et les « Lignes Directrices »  de la Banque mondiale sur la Prévention et la Lutte contre la Fraude et la Corruption dans les projets financés sur les Prêts de la BIRD, et les crédits et les subventions de l’IDA (datant du 1er juillet 2016), ainsi que les dispositions stipulées dans l’Accord de financement applicables au projet.

8. Les Consultants intéressés et remplissant les conditions requises, peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures suivantes :  E-mail : dpm@star-rdc.org  avec copie à : recrutementstarest@yahoo.com; aayumbi_yumbiali@yahoo.com

Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être envoyées par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (en personne, par courrier, par fax ou par e-mail) au plus tard le 04 août 2026 à 16 heures précises, heures locales de la ville de Kinshasa (GMT+2) et porter clairement la mention : « ZR-STAR EST-551995-CS-QCBS : « Recrutement d’un partenaire facilitateur pour appuyer le Projet STAR RDC dans la réalisation des activités des Travaux à Haute Intensité de Main d’œuvre (THIMO) dans les Provinces du Kwango, Kwilu et Mai-Ndombe».

 

A Madame Brigitte KAPINGA SAUDA

procnotices.notice_text:
FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF SOMALIA

 Somalia National Bureau of Statistics

SOMALI INTEGRATED STATISTICS AND ECONOMIC PLANNING CAPACITY BUILDING  

PROJECT (SISEPCBP) 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)  

  INDIVIDUAL SELECTION OF CONSULTANT  

Country: Federal Government of Somalia 

Name of the Project: Somali Integrated Statistics and Economic Planning Capacity Building Project (SISEPCBP) 

Consulting Service: SNBS Senior Executive Assistant

Individual/Firm: Individual 

Duty Station: Somalia National Bureau of Statistics, FGS, Mogadishu -Somalia  

Deadline: 31st July, 2026

Ref No. SO-SNBS-559889-CS-INDV

1. Background of the project  

 The Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), through the Somali National Bureau of Statistics (SNBS), has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) to implement the Somali Integrated Statistics and Economic Capacity Building (SISEPCB) Project.  The proposed project aims at strengthening the national statistics system, the national monitoring and evaluation (M&E) system and improving programming and analytical capacity of the government’s macroeconomics and fiscal programming agencies to enable them to regularly access analyze and improve their public policies and programs performance and results. More specifically, the project aims at: (1) Strengthening the national statistics system; (2) Strengthening monitoring and evaluation capacity; and (3) Building economic policy analysis and economic planning capacity. 

2. Responsibilities

The SNBS Executive Secretary will carry out all the duties and may also take a greater role in the day-to-day administration office. It will support also the oversee in ensuring the smooth functioning of the office Management duties, including drafting routine correspondence, typing, word processing, scheduling appointments, establishing and maintaining files and records. The detailed ToR for the assignment can be found at the following Website: https://nbs.gov.so/vacancies/  or https://sisepcbp.nbs.gov.so/jobs-tenders/ or can be provided upon submission of the application in person or by e-mail. The e-mail address is provided below. 

3. Selection criteria

The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include: 

  • University Degree in Public Administration, economics, Public Policy or related field.
  • A minimum of five years’ working experience in administration or office management. The candidate should have knowledge and understanding of office administration and public relations.

4. Reporting 

The executive secretary will report to the SNBS Director General.

 5. Duration of assignment 

 The estimated duration of the assignment is 12 Months.

 The Somalia National Bureau of Statistics now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the Services and furnish the Curriculum Vitae (CV).  

6. Submission requirements  

 Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 “Procurement Regulations”, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIQUE DU TCHAD                                                                                           PRESIDENCE DE LAREPUBLIQUE

 PRIMATURE

MINISTERE DES TRANSPORTS, DE L’AVIATION CIVILE ET DE LA METEOROLOGIE NATIONALE

SECRETARIAT GENERAL

PROJET DE CONNECTIVITE ET D’INTEGRATION DU TCHAD

SERVICE PASSATION DES MARCHES

Unité- Travail-Progrès   --

             

 

   

 

 

PROJET DE CONNECTIVITE ET D’INTEGRATION DUTCHAD

Financement : Crédit IDA E4110-TD Agence fiduciaire : PCIT

 

 

SOLLICITATION A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET N°_________MTACMN/SG/PCIT/SPM/2026

Pour le recrutement d’un Bureau d’Études chargé de réaliser l’étude de faisabilité portant sur la modernisation de la navigabilité du Lac Tchad et des fleuves Chari et Logone

 

I. Contexte du Projet

Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad a obtenu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour la mise en œuvre du Projet de Connectivité et d’Intégration du Tchad (PCIT). L’objectif du projet est d’améliorer la connectivité multimodale et la logistique afin de soutenir le développement des chaînes de valeur à fort potentiel économique dans le bassin du Lac Tchad.

À cet effet, il est prévu le recrutement d’un Bureau d’Études spécialisé pour réaliser une étude de faisabilité technique, économique, financière, environnementale et sociale portant sur la modernisation de la navigabilité du Lac Tchad et des fleuves Chari et Logone.

II. Objectif de la mission

II.1. Objectif global

Réaliser une étude de faisabilité complète permettant d’évaluer les conditions techniques, économiques, environnementales et sociales nécessaires à l’amélioration durable de la navigabilité sur le Lac Tchad et les fleuves Chari et Logone.

II.2. Objectifs spécifiques

Le Bureau d’Études devra notamment :

  • Évaluer les conditions actuelles de navigation sur le Lac Tchad et les fleuves Chari et Logone ;
  • Identifier les contraintes physiques, hydrologiques, hydrauliques, environnementales et institutionnelles affectant la navigabilité ;
  • Réaliser les études techniques nécessaires à l’amélioration des voies navigables ;
  • Identifier les aménagements et infrastructures requis pour le développement du transport fluvial et lacustre ;
  • Évaluer la viabilité économique et financière des investissements proposés ;
  • Analyser les impacts environnementaux et sociaux des aménagements envisagés ;
  •  Élaborer un programme d’investissements assorti d’un plan de mise en œuvre et d’entretien des infrastructures.

III. Résultats attendus

La mission devra permettre de produire les résultats suivants :

  • Un diagnostic complet de l’état actuel de la navigabilité du Lac Tchad et des fleuves Chari et Logone ;
  • Une analyse des conditions hydrologiques, hydrauliques et bathymétriques des zones concernées ;
  • L’identification et la caractérisation des principaux obstacles à la navigation ;
  • Des scénarios techniques d’amélioration de la navigabilité accompagnés d’analyses comparatives ;
  • Une étude de faisabilité technique, économique et financière des options retenues ;
  • Une évaluation des impacts environnementaux et sociaux des investissements proposés ;
  • Un plan d’investissement priorisé assorti d’un calendrier de mise en œuvre ;
  • Les rapports d’études validés par l’Autorité Contractante et les parties prenantes concernées.

IV. Durée et déroulement de la mission

La durée indicative de la mission est de douze (12) mois.

V. Tâches principales du Consultant

Le Bureau d’Études devra notamment :

  • Mobiliser une équipe pluridisciplinaire composée notamment d’experts en transport fluvial, hydrologie, hydraulique, génie civil, environnement, développement social et économie des transports ;
  • Réaliser les investigations et collectes de données nécessaires à l’étude ;
  • Effectuer les levés topographiques, bathymétriques, hydrologiques et hydrauliques requis ;
  • Identifier les infrastructures existantes et les besoins en aménagements complémentaires ;
  • Évaluer les besoins en dragage, balisage, signalisation et infrastructures portuaires ou débarcadères ;
  • Réaliser les analyses économiques et financières des investissements proposés ;
  • Préparer les études environnementales et sociales conformément aux exigences nationales et aux standards de la Banque mondiale ;
  • Organiser les consultations des parties prenantes et les ateliers de validation ;
  • Produire et soumettre les rapports d’étapes, les rapports provisoires et le rapport final conformément au calendrier convenu.

VI. Modalités de sélection

Les Consultants intéressés doivent démontrer leurs qualifications, leurs expériences et leurs capacités techniques par la réalisation de missions similaires. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont les suivants :

  • Les Consultants (Firmes) doivent être des bureaux d’études ou cabinets spécialisés disposant d’au moins dix (10) années d’expérience générale dans les études d’infrastructures de transport, de navigation fluviale, de transport multimodal ou de gestion des voies navigables ;
  • Les Consultants (Firmes) doivent avoir réalisé avec succès, au cours des dix (10) dernières années, au moins cinq (05) missions similaires portant sur des études de faisabilité, études techniques ou études relatives au transport fluvial, lacustre, portuaire ou multimodal ;
  • Une expérience dans le cadre de projets financés par des institutions internationales telles que la Banque mondiale, la Banque Africaine de Développement (BAD), la Banque Islamique de Développement (BID), l’Union Européenne ou d’autres partenaires techniques et financiers constituera un atout ;

Les références présentées devront être justifiées par des attestations de bonne exécution ou de bonne fin ainsi que par les documents contractuels pertinents.

La sélection sera conduite conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition de septembre 2025.

Le Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur les Qualifications du Consultant (SQC).

VII. Dépôt des candidatures et informations complémentaires

Les candidats intéressés peuvent obtenir les Termes de Référence (TdR) et des informations complémentaires aux heures suivantes : Du lundi au jeudi de 08h30 à 15h00 et le vendredi de 08h30 à 11h00 Les dossiers de candidature, sous pli fermé doivent être déposés au plus tard le   03 aout 2026 à l’adresse suivante :

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

 

West and Central Africa

Regional Program for Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Solutions (Regional DARES)

Project ID: P507938

Credit No.:8080-LR

 

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for RCU Productive Uses of Energy (PUE) Expert

 

Reference No.: LR-RCU-DARES-557728-CS-INDV

 

The Governments of Liberia, Sierra Leone, Benin, and Central Africa Republic have received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Program for Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Solutions (Regional DARES) and intend to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services ("the Services") will ensure that productiveuse considerations are systematically embedded across Program components, enabling strong alignment between electricity access investments and incomegenerating economic activities in sectors such as agriculture, agroprocessing, rural enterprises, and emerging digital services.. The duration of the assignment is approximately five years, with an expected start in October 2026.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link: https://lecliberia.com/wp-content/uploads/R-DARES-TOR-POE-PUE-Expert-.docx

 

The RESPITE Regional Coordination Unit (RCU) now invites eligible and selected Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should submit their Expressions of Interest (EOI), including their CV with information demonstrating that they are qualified to perform the services (description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills, etc.), educational and professional qualification certificates.

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s level or equivalent) in energy, engineering, agriculture, rural development, economics, business, or a closely related field.
  • At least 8–10 years of relevant professional experience in productive use of energy, rural development, agribusiness, or related sectors;
  • Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, or assessing productiveuse interventions linked to energy access programs;
  • Experience conducting valuechain analysis and identifying commercially viable productiveuse opportunities;
  • Excellent knowledge of productiveuse equipment and their energy requirements (e.g., agroprocessing, irrigation, cold chains, smallscale manufacturing);
  • Experience working with privatesector actors, including DRE companies, agribusinesses, equipment suppliers, and financial institutions;
  • Demonstrated understanding of market development challenges specific to PUE segments in Sub-Saharan Africa, including barriers to adoption, competitive landscape, demand-side constraints, financing gaps, and policy environment, across at least two of the three technology windows under Regional DARES: solar irrigation, solar cooling, and agro-processing;
  • Experience structuring or supporting resultsbased or performancebased programs is an advantage;
  • Experience working in SubSaharan Africa, including fragile environments, is highly desirable;
  • Familiarity with World Bank or other MDBfinanced operations is a strong advantage.

 

The shortlisted candidates will be informed via email and invited for a virtual interview.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.11 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (Procurement Regulations”) as available on https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/c84273d1b230aeb2b0b8134de5dc8cd7-0290012025/original/Procurement-Regulations-7th-Edition-Sep-2025.pdf, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 0900 to 1700 hours GMT.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by email or by physical mail on or before Friday, August 7, 2026.

 

RCU PROJECT COORDINATOR

RESPITE Coordination Unit

15th Street & Warner Avenue

Sinkor, Monrovia, Liberia

Email: f.kyere@respite-rcu.org and copied s.hedd-williams@respite-rcu.org

1. O Governo de Moçambique, através do Ministério das Finanças recebeu um crédito da Associação Internacional de Desenvolvimento (IDA) para financiar os custos do Projecto de Acesso ao Financiamento e Oportunidades Económicas (Mais Oportunidades) e pretende utilizar parte dos fundos para cobrir pagamentos elegíveis nos termos do Contrato para o Aluguer de Viaturas para Apoio as Actividades do Projecto Moz Materiais Beneficiário: Ministério das Obras Públicas, Habitação e Recursos Hídricos – Laboratório de Engenharia de Moçambique (LEM, IP).

 

2. O Ministério das Finanças, convida os concorrentes de países elegíveis e qualificados a apresentarem propostas seladas para Aluguer de Viaturas para Apoio as Actividades do Projecto Moz Materiais. Os concorrentes devem cotar todos os itens.

 

3. O Concurso será regido pelos procedimentos de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários sob Financiamento de Projectos de Investimento, revisto em Setembro de 2023 e as disposições estipuladas no Acordo de Financiamento e o mesmo está aberto a todos concorrentes de países elegíveis conforme estabelecido nos Documentos de Concurso.

 

4. Os concorrentes interessados poderão obter mais informações e apreciar os Documentos de Concurso no endereço abaixo, em horário de expediente entre as 8:00h às 15:30h.

 

5. Os requisitos para qualificação incluem: prova documental da capacidade técnica, financeira, jurídica e outros critérios mencionados nos Documentos de Concurso. O volume médio anual de negócios nos últimos 3 anos deverá ser de pelo menos 14.200.000 MT e ter executado pelo menos dois contratos similares (em valor e natureza) nos últimos cinco anos. A margem de preferência para os fornecedores nacionais elegíveis não será aplicada. Detalhes adicionais são fornecidos nos Documentos de Concurso.

 

6. Os Documentos de Concurso em Português pode ser adquirido por concorrentes elegíveis interessados mediante solicitação por escrito para o seguinte e-mail: procurement.pled@gmail.com. Os Documentos de Concurso poderão ser levantados no endereço abaixo ou enviados por correio expresso por conta dos concorrentes interessados.

 

7. As propostas deverão ser entregues no endereço abaixo até às 10:30 horas do dia 18 de Agosto de 2026. Propostas em versão electrónica não serão aceites. As propostas serão abertas na presença dos representantes dos concorrentes que desejarem assistir a abertura no endereço abaixo indicado às 10:30 horas do dia 18 de Agosto de 2026.

 

8. As propostas deverão ser válidas pelo período de 120 (cento e vinte) dias e devem ser acompanhadas por uma Garantia Bancária Provisória no valor de 140,000.00 MZN (cento e quarenta mil meticais), válidas pelo período de 148 (cento e quarenta e oito) dias.

procnotices.bid_description: Organization and Delivery of I_CAN Training Program Sessions No. 1–2 in Khmelnytskyi, No. 3–4 in Ternopil and No. 5 in Kyiv
procnotices.notice_text:
SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Request for Quotations

Country: Ukraine

Name of Project: Center for Advancement in Restoration and Modernization Capacity Project

Contract Title:  Organization and Delivery of I_CAN Training Program Sessions No. 1–2 in Khmelnytskyi, No. 3–4 in Ternopil and No. 5 in Kyiv

Grant No.: TF0C4831

RFB Reference No.: NCS-RFQ-2.5-8

1.         The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Development Association (the World Bank) and Kyiv School of Economics Institute (KSEI) have signed the Grant Agreement No. TF0C4831 dated May 7, 2024, in an amount not to exceed three million two hundred twelve thousand United States Dollars (USD 3,212,000) for the Project ‘Center for Advancement in Restoration and Modernization Capacity (CARMC)’ (hereinafter referred to as the I_CAN Project). The KSEI is the implementing entity for the Project. A portion of these funds is intended to cover expenditures under the contract for the financing of logistical support for event organization.

2.         The KSEI now invites Quotations from eligible Service providers for:

Organization and Delivery of I_CAN Training Program Sessions No. 1–2 in Khmelnytskyi, No. 3–4 in Ternopil and No. 5 in Kyiv:

The procurement is organized into a single lot, resulting in the award of one contract upon completion of the tender process.

Services shall be rendered during August, 2026.

Planned events dates:

  • 10.08.2026 - 13.08.2026- training No. 1 (Khmelnytskyi);
  • 11.08.2026 - 14.08.2026 - training No. 2 (Khmelnytskyi);
  • 17.08.2026 - 20.08.2026 - training No. 3 (Ternopil);
  • 18.08.2026 - 21.08.2026 - training No. 4 (Ternopil);
  • 25.08.2026 - 28.08.2026 - training No. 5 (Kyiv);

The prospective Service providers shall meet the following Qualification Criteria:

Experience:

            - the Service provider must have experience in the execution of at least 1 (one) contract for the provision of comprehensive logistical support services for conferences, training sessions, or similar events within the last 3 (three) years, specifically since January 1, 2023;

- the Service provider must not be subject to ongoing bankruptcy proceedings and/or be in a state of insolvency as of the date of the price quotation submission, in accordance with the provisions of the legislation of Ukraine.

Evaluation will be conducted based on comparing price quotations received from Service providers.

Detailed information is described in the Request for Quotations (the Tender Documents).

3.         The tender will be conducted through national competitive procurement using a Request for Quotations (RFQ) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (September, 2023) (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Service providers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

The KSE shall use the following electronic-procurement system to manage this Tender process:

“Electronic procurement system” or “e-procurement system” means national electronic procurement system “Prozorro” available at https://prozorro.gov.ua/, including authorized electronic procurement marketplaces.

The full list of authorized electronic marketplaces is available at https://prozorro.gov.ua/en/majdanchiki-prozorro.

In order to submit the Quotations and/or request clarifications, the Participants shall register at one of the authorized electronic marketplaces of Participant’s choice in accordance with terms and conditions of selected marketplace.

4.         The full set of Tender documents in Ukrainian, including addenda and clarifications thereof, if any, is published by the KSE at the website of electronic procurement system and will be available for free for downloading at the following link:

https://prozorro.gov.ua/uk/tender/UA-2026-07-16-003495-a

5.         Quotations must be submitted by uploading the complete tender documents through the electronic-procurement system before the quotations submission deadline which is 17:00 (Kyiv time) on July 27, 2026. After the deadline the participants will not be able to submit the quotations and this option will be closed by the system automatically.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

 

West and Central Africa

Regional Program for Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Solutions (Regional DARES)

Project ID: P507938

Credit No.:8080-LR

 

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Provision of Regional Coordinating Unit Manager, Full-Time (International)

Reference No.: LR-RCU-DARES-557714-CS-INDV

 

The Governments of Liberia, Sierra Leone, Benin, and Central Africa Republic have received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Program for Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Solutions (Regional DARES) and intend to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") include strategic coordination, contract and performance oversight, fiduciary and safeguards supervision, monitoring and reporting, and stakeholder engagement across participating countries (Liberia, Sierra Leone, Central Africa Republic, and Benin). The duration of the assignment is approximately five years, with an expected start in October 2026.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link: https://lecliberia.com/wp-content/uploads/R-DARES-TOR-RCU-Head.docx

 

The RESPITE Regional Coordination Unit (RCU) now invites eligible and selected Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should submit their Expressions of Interest (EOI), including their CV with information demonstrating that they are qualified to perform the services (description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills, etc.), educational and professional qualification certificates, etc.

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • Advanced university degree (minimum Master’s level) in business administration, economics, engineering, energy, public policy, international development, or another relevant discipline.
  • At least 15 years of post-qualification professional experience, including a minimum of 8–10 years in the energy sector or infrastructure development in a reputable organization, Government agency, or other donor-funded projects;
  • At least 7 years’ experience in senior coordination, program management, or leadership roles within public institutions, development finance–supported programs, or donor-funded projects;
  • Demonstrated experience managing multi-country, multi-stakeholder programs;
  • Experience working with World Bank or other multilateral development bank–financed operations, including familiarity with procurement, fiduciary, and safeguards frameworks;
  • Demonstrated experience in contract management and supervision at a senior level;
  • Knowledge of energy sector strategic issues and policies in participating countries is an asset.

 

The shortlisted candidates will be informed via email and invited for a virtual interview.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (Procurement Regulations”) as available on https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/c84273d1b230aeb2b0b8134de5dc8cd7-0290012025/original/Procurement-Regulations-7th-Edition-Sep-2025.pdf, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 0900 to 1700 hours GMT.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by email or by physical mail on or before Friday, August 7, 2026.

 

RCU PROJECT COORDINATOR

RESPITE Coordination Unit

15th Street & Warner Avenue

Sinkor, Monrovia, Liberia

Email: f.kyere@respite-rcu.org and copied s.hedd-williams@respite-rcu.org

Specific Procurement Notice

Request for Bids

Small Works

(One-Envelope Bidding Process)

Country: Albania

Name of Project: Building Resilient Bridges

Contract Title: Rehabilitation Works of Murrashi Bridge

Loan No.: 94790-AL

RFB Reference No.: AL-ARA-531200-CW-RFB

1. The Government of Albania has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Building Resilient Bridges Project (BRBP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for the civil works for Rehabilitation Works of Murrashi Bridge. Procurement process will be governed by the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.

2. The Albanian Road Authority hereby invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for the rehabilitation of the Murashi Bridge, located in the Elbasan region. The works under this contract consist of rehabilitation and repair of the existing bridge structure and associated elements, including deck rehabilitation, localized structural repairs, drainage improvements, and sidewalks. No demolition of the main bridge structure or construction of a new bridge is foreseen under this contract. The contract duration is twelve (12) months, followed by a Defects Liability Period of twelve (12) months. Qualification requirements are set out in the Bidding Documents. Bidders shall meet the minimum qualification criteria specified therein.

a. The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has access to, or has available, liquid assets, unencumbered real assets, lines of credit, and other financial means (independent of any contractual advance payment) sufficient to meet the construction cash flow requirements estimated as one hundred thousand (100.000) Euro for the subject contract(s) net of the Bidder’s other commitments. 

b. The Bidders shall also demonstrate, to the satisfaction of the Employer, that it has adequate sources of finance to meet the cash flow requirements on works currently in progress and for future contract commitments.

c. The audited balance sheets or, if not required by the laws of the Bidder’s country, other financial statements acceptable to the Employer, for the last three (3) years prior to the deadline of submission (i.e. 2023, 2024, 2025), shall be submitted and must demonstrate the current soundness of the Bidder’s financial position and indicate its prospective long-term profitability.

d. Minimum average annual construction turnover of five hundred thousand (500,000) Euro, calculated as total certified payments received for contracts in progress and/or completed within the three (3) years prior the deadline of submission (i.e. 2023, 2024, 2025), divided by three (3) years.

e. Experience under construction contracts in the role of prime contractor, JV member, subcontractor, or management contractor for at least the last five (5) years, prior to the deadline of submission.

f. A minimum number of similar contracts specified below that have been satisfactorily and substantially completed as a prime contractor, joint venture member, management contractor or sub-contractor6 between 1st January 2021 and bid submission deadline: Three (3) contracts, each of minimum value 200,000 Euro. Or Less than or equal to 3 contracts each of minimum value or 200,000 Euro but with total value of all contracts equal or more than 600,000 Euro. The similarity of the contracts shall be based on Section VII, Scope of Works, specify the minimum key requirements in terms of physical size, complexity, construction method, technology and/or other characteristics including part of the requirements.

g. For the above and any other contracts substantially completed and under implementation as prime contractor, joint venture member, or sub-contractor between 1st January 2021 and Application submission deadline, a minimum construction experience in the following key activities successfully completed.

  • Bridge deck rehabilitation works with a minimum cumulative treated deck area ≥ 500 m²;
  • Structural concrete repair works on bridges or similar structures with a minimum cumulative repaired surface ≥ 500 m²;

3. Bidding will be conducted through national competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, dated  July 2016 as amended on  November 2020, (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from Albanian Road Authority  and inspect the bidding document during office 08:00 to 16:30 (Monday to Thursday) and 08:00 to 14:00 on Friday  at the address given below.

5. The bidding document in English may be purchased by interested eligible Bidders upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a nonrefundable fee of 10.000 Albanian Lek. The method of payment will be a direct deposit to the ARA though the Albanian Treasury at the following account:

  • The Bank:              CREDINS BANK,
  • Account Name:     NDERTIMI I URAVE TE QENDRUESHME
  • SWIFT Code:        CDISALTRXXXX
  • Account Number:  00002015360
  • Iban:                      AL04212110090000000002015360

The bidding document will be sent by email or dispatched and consist of:

  • Volume I:   The request for Bids (RFB)
  • Volume II:  Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP)
  • Volume III: Drawings/Design

6. Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before August 28, 2026 not later than 10:00 am local time. Electronic Bidding will not be permitted. Late Bids will be rejected. Bids will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend at the address below on August 28, 2026 not later than 10:10 am local time.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

 

West and Central Africa

Regional Program for Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Solutions (Regional DARES)

Project ID: P507938

Credit No.:8080-LR

 

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for RCU Environmental, Social and GBV Coordinator

 

Reference No.: LR-RCU-DARES-557715-CS-INDV

 

The Governments of Liberia, Sierra Leone, Benin, and Central Africa Republic have received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Program for Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Solutions (Regional DARES) and intend to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") will involve coordinating the design and implementation of environmental and social risk management plans with institutions involved in DARES at both regional and country levels. Ongoing assessment and monitoring of compliance with the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) for each country, which are essential, with proactive identification and resolution of non-compliance issues, including timely reporting to the World Bank on any delays or problems relating to ESCP obligations. The duration of the assignment is approximately five years, with an expected start in October 2026.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link: https://lecliberia.com/wp-content/uploads/R-DARES-TOR-RCU-ES-Cordinator-Final.docx      

 

The RESPITE Regional Coordination Unit (RCU) now invites eligible and selected Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should submit their Expressions of Interest (EOI), including their CV with information demonstrating that they are qualified to perform the services (description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills, etc.), educational and professional qualification certificates.

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • The environmental and social Coordinator must have at least an MSc. Social sciences, Environmental Sciences or Engineering for the Environmental Manager or equivalent, or any other related field of social or environmental studies.
  • At least fifteen (15) years of relevant work experience with bilateral and/or multilateral development projects in environmental or social risk management, monitoring and reporting, including the design and/or implementation of ESMPs, RAPs, Cultural Heritage plans, Labour procedures, SEPs, and/or Security Management Plans, among others. Of the 15 years of relevant E&S work experience, at least 5 is required to have been in an international assignment. Experience in implementing E&S risk management in a Bank financed project/program is an added advantage.
  • At least 5 years’ experience with management of a team of 5 or more people.
  • E&S risk management in the energy sector is an added advantage. 
  • Demonstrated experience on the design and implementation of inclusive approaches to consultation and participation with diverse stakeholders, including government counterparts, private sector, civil society organizations and/or local communities.
  • Working experience of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) is required.
  • Demonstrated experience of managing both Environment and Social risk including gender-based violence, sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.
  • Proven experience and familiarity with the sub-Saharan African region.
  • Proven experience in preparing and delivering capacity building and training programs
  • The candidate must be computer literate, with high proficiency in Computer software operations (Microsoft Word, Excel, Power-Point and data-base management etc.).

 

The shortlisted candidates will be informed via email and invited for a virtual interview.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.11 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (Procurement Regulations”) as available on https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/c84273d1b230aeb2b0b8134de5dc8cd7-0290012025/original/Procurement-Regulations-7th-Edition-Sep-2025.pdf, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Extension of deadline for submission of EoI:

Please refer to the below SPN, the EOI submission deadline has been extended to 05 August 2026. Now the Expression of Interest needs to be submitted in a written form (either through e-mail or in person or by mail) to the following address by 15:00 hours (Bhutan Time) (GMT + 6 hours) on or before 05 August, 2026.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 Country: Kingdom of Bhutan

Name of Project: Accelerating Transport and Trade Connectivity in Eastern South Asia (Access) – Bhutan Project

Loan No/Credit No/ Grant No: IDA 77560 (Credit)/IDAE4310 (grant)

Assignment Title: Selection of Consultant for Conducting the Integrated Geohazard Assessment (IGA) for Mangdechhu and Drangmechhu River Basins

Reference No: DGPC/ACCESS/IGA/2025/12

  1. Royal Government of Bhutan has received financial assistance in the form of Credit and Grant from the World Bank towards the cost of the proposed Accelerating Transport and Trade Connectivity in Eastern South Asia (ACCESS)-Bhutan Project, to be implemented partly by the Department of Surface Transport (DoST), Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport (MoIT), and intends to apply a part of the proceeds of this financing for the services of “Selection of Consultant for Conducting the Integrated Geohazard Assessment (IGA) for Mangdechhu and Drangmechhu River Basins”.

2. Scope of Services 

The scope of work comprises an Integrated Geohazard Assessment (IGA) of the Mangdechhu River Basin (Mangdechhu and Chamkharchhu rivers) and the Drangmechhu River Basin (Kurichhu and Gongrichhu rivers) in central and eastern Bhutan, to support the planning and preparation of hydropower projects in these basins, including the Dorjilung Hydroelectric Power Plant. The assignment will evaluate geological, hydro-meteorological, and cryosphere-related hazards under current and future climate scenarios to identify risk-informed measures that strengthen dam safety and the long-term resilience of hydropower infrastructure. Key activities include an inception workshop and comprehensive desk study of existing geohazard, seismic, hydrological, and climate-risk information; a gap analysis to identify outstanding data and field investigation needs; and a comprehensive IGA covering event mapping, process identification, neo-tectonic and regional geological analysis, and a glacial hazard assessment — including an inventory of glaciers and glacial lakes, hazard ranking, detailed feasibility and numerical breach/flood modelling for at least two high-hazard glacial lakes, and recommendations for future monitoring. The 18-month assignment will be delivered through an Interim IGA Report for the Kurichhu/Dorjilung sub-basin, a Draft IGA Report covering both river basins, and a Final IGA Report, supported by at least three visits to Bhutan, including an Inception Workshop and an IGA Workshop.

3. Detail Terms of Reference (TOR) will be available in https://www.drukgreen.bt/tender/ from June 29, 2026.

4. The DoST, MoIT represented by Druk Green Power Corporation Ltd (DGPC) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • General Experience of the Consultant in providing similar services (core business and years in business);
  • Experience in similar assignments of compatible size, complexity and technical specialty in the required area;
  • Experience in working with development partner financed projects; and
  • Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including overall staffing and logistics.

Consultants are requested to submit, but not limited to, the following supporting documents in support of the above-mentioned criteria:

  1. The Firm's Incorporation/Trade/registration documents from the country of the firm
  2. Firm’s brochures;
  3. Description of similar consultancy contracts, including the scope, contract amount, name of Client, period of the contract (date of contract signing to date of completion), location/ country of the services, etc.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment as per paragraph 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations: Consultants shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower.

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or a sub-consultancy (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultant must explain in the EoI submission (a) the rationale/ justification for the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants; and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment. Failure to provide the above explanation in the EoI may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. However, the qualifications/ experience of sub-consultants will not be considered in the evaluation of Expressions of Interest for Shortlisting. The total number of firms in the association will be limited to a maximum of Three (03).

7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

8. Expected date for commencement of the services is February 2027 and the duration of the assignment is eighteen (18) months.

9. The Expression of Interest needs to be submitted in a written form (either through e-mail or in person or by mail) to the following address by 15:00 hours (Bhutan Time) (GMT + 6 hours) on or before July 22, 2026. Please clearly mention “Expression of Interest (EoI) for “Selection of Consultant for Conducting the Integrated Geohazard Assessment (IGA) for Mangdechhu and Drangmechhu River Basins” in the e-mail’s subject line or on the top of the envelope.

10. Further information can be obtained at the address mentioned below during office hours between 0900 to 1700 hours Bhutan Standard Time. DGPC reserves the right to accept or reject any or all EOIs without assigning any reason, whatsoever.

Country: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

Name of Project: Project Preparation Support for a proposed project “Agriculture Value Chain Development for Climate Resilience and Jobs in Ethiopia (P510576)

Grant No.: E5760

Assignment Title: Individual Consultancy Service for Recruitment of Procurement Expert for procurement Assessment and Development of Procurement manual and Guidelines RFB Reference No: (ET-MOLF-551203-CS-INDV)

Employer: Ministry of Agriculture

The Government of Ethiopia, through the Ministry of Agriculture, is implementing the six-year Agriculture Value Chains Development for Resilience, Commercialization and Jobs (AVC4Jobs) project to enhance the competitiveness of strategic agricultural value chains, improve livelihood resilience, and create employment opportunities for youth and women by strengthening sustainable production systems and market linkages. The project intends to finance Individual Consulting services for the recruitment of a Procurement Expert to support procurement assessment and the development of procurement manuals and guidelines

The objective of this individual consultancy service is to Conduct a comprehensive fiduciary assessment of procurement systems, procedures, staffing, and capacity across federal, regional, and woreda levels; provide targeted recommendations to mitigate gaps and risks and improve transparency and efficiency; develop and finalize procurement management manuals, operational guidelines, and a project procurement strategy; build capacity of the core design and implementation teams and Ministry staff through targeted training on procurement standards and best practices; and prepare an 18month procurement plan to support effective project design and implementation.

The following specific tasks are expected from the individual consultant; specifically:

  • Procurement Management Capacity Assessment and Recommendations
  • Development of Procurement Manuals and Operational Guidelines 
  • Capacity Building and Training on Procurement Management 
  • Preparation of PPSD and 18-month PP.

Duration of the Service

The individual consultant will be required to complete the services within 12 weeks from the date of the effectiveness of the contract.

Qualification and Experience

Education

  • A minimum of first degree in Economics, Management, Accounting, Business Administration, procurement and supply management, engineering, law or other related disciplines;

Experience

  • Good knowledge of standard procurement methods and procedures;
  • Ten (10) years relevant working experience, of which five years continuous experience is in procurement management at senior level, and 3 years’ experience on the World Bank financed projects;
  • Knowledge and experience off World Bank procurement procedures and World Bank regulation as well as Ethiopian Government procurement procedures and documentation will be an added advantage.
  • Knowledge and experience in use of STEP system
  • Experience in successful execution of procurement capacity assessment, procurement audit
  • Experience in preparation of PPSD
  • Fluency in written and spoken English.
  • Excellent analytical skills and report writing.

The Consultant will be hired as individual local consultant with relevant qualification and experience for the assignment.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained from the clients address depicted here under or can be accessed on request from belay.tariku@moa.gov.et or/tamrat.tefassa@moa.gov.et

The attention of interested individual Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised September 2025; seventh edition, Procurement in IPF Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services(“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

procnotices.notice_text:
SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Request for Quotations

Country: Ukraine

Name of Project: Center for Advancement in Restoration and Modernization Capacity Project

Contract Title:  Organization and Delivery of I_CAN Training Program Sessions No. 1–2 in Rivne and No. 3–4 in Uzhhorod

Grant No.: TF0C4831

RFB Reference No.: NCS-RFQ-2.5-9

1.         The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Development Association (the World Bank) and Kyiv School of Economics Institute (KSEI) have signed the Grant Agreement No. TF0C4831 dated May 7, 2024, in an amount not to exceed three million two hundred twelve thousand United States Dollars (USD 3,212,000) for the Project ‘Center for Advancement in Restoration and Modernization Capacity (CARMC)’ (hereinafter referred to as the I_CAN Project). The KSEI is the implementing entity for the Project. A portion of these funds is intended to cover expenditures under the contract for the financing of logistical support for event organization.

2.         The KSEI now invites Quotations from eligible Service providers for:

Organization and Delivery of I_CAN Training Program Sessions No. 1–2 in Rivne and No. 3–4 in Uzhhorod:

The procurement is organized into a single lot, resulting in the award of one contract upon completion of the tender process.

Services shall be rendered during August - September, 2026.

Planned events dates:

  • 31.08.2026 - 03.09.2026 - training No. 1 (Rivne);
  • 01.09.2026 - 04.09.2026 - training No. 2 (Rivne);
  • 28.09.2026 -01.10.2026  - training No. 3 (Uzhhorod);
  • 29.09.2026 - 02.10.2026  - training No. 4 (Uzhhorod).

The prospective Service providers shall meet the following Qualification Criteria:

Experience:

            - the Service provider must have experience in the execution of at least 1 (one) contract for the provision of comprehensive logistical support services for conferences, training sessions, or similar events within the last 3 (three) years, specifically since January 1, 2023;

- the Service provider must not be subject to ongoing bankruptcy proceedings and/or be in a state of insolvency as of the date of the price quotation submission, in accordance with the provisions of the legislation of Ukraine.

Evaluation will be conducted based on comparing price quotations received from Service providers.

Detailed information is described in the Request for Quotations (the Tender Documents).

3.         The tender will be conducted through national competitive procurement using a Request for Quotations (RFQ) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (September, 2023) (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Service providers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

The KSE shall use the following electronic-procurement system to manage this Tender process:

“Electronic procurement system” or “e-procurement system” means national electronic procurement system “Prozorro” available at https://prozorro.gov.ua/, including authorized electronic procurement marketplaces.

The full list of authorized electronic marketplaces is available at https://prozorro.gov.ua/en/majdanchiki-prozorro.

In order to submit the Quotations and/or request clarifications, the Participants shall register at one of the authorized electronic marketplaces of Participant’s choice in accordance with terms and conditions of selected marketplace.

4.         The full set of Tender documents in Ukrainian, including addenda and clarifications thereof, if any, is published by the KSE at the website of electronic procurement system and will be available for free for downloading at the following link:

https://prozorro.gov.ua/uk/tender/UA-2026-07-16-003953-a

5.         Quotations must be submitted by uploading the complete tender documents through the electronic-procurement system before the quotations submission deadline which is 17:00 (Kyiv time) on July  31, 2026. After the deadline the participants will not be able to submit the quotations and this option will be closed by the system automatically.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT - CIVIL ENGINEER (PART-TIME))

Republic of North Macedonia

Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy

Agriculture Modernization Project

Loan No.: 9037-MK

Assignment Title: Individual Consultant - Civil Engineer (part-time)

Reference No.: AMP-IC-3.7-1

The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy of the Republic of North Macedonia (MAFWE) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Agriculture Modernization Project (AMP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Project aims to improve competitiveness in targeted agricultural sub-sectors and strengthen agricultural public sector readiness for EU accession.

The main objective of this assignment is to oversee the building and reconstruction activities implemented under Sub-component 1.2 - Agriculture and Food Distribution Systems and Sub-component 2.2 - IPARD Implementation Capacity. The assignment relates primarily to the Collection and Conditioning Center (CCC) in Strumica municipality, the Agri-Food Platform (AFP) in the Skopje suburban area, and the renovation and adaptation of the office building intended to accommodate the increased needs of the Agency for Financial Support in Agriculture and Rural Development (AFSARD).

The consulting services ("the Services") include drafting Terms of Reference for supervision of construction activities and supporting procurement documentation, including technical specifications and bills of quantities (BoQs); reviewing designs, permits and technical documentation; monitoring and reporting on compliance with national legislation, building standards and contractual requirements; supporting verification of completed works and the quality of materials used; reviewing reports submitted by supervision and works contractors; conducting site visits; liaising with relevant authorities; participating in evaluation committees; and assisting in negotiations with contractors. The Civil Engineer will closely cooperate with the other Civil Engineer engaged within the AMP Project Management Team and will report to the Project Director and Project Coordinator.

The Civil Engineer is expected to work part-time under a time-based contract arrangement, with an estimated input of 100 man-days over a period of sixteen (16) months. The assignment is expected to commence in September 2026 and continue until the Project Closing Date in December 2027. The contract will include an initial probationary period of three (3) months. The Services will be performed at the premises of MAFWE and, as required, at the relevant construction sites.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment is posted on the website of MAFWE at the following link: www.amp.mk

MAFWE now invites eligible individuals ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information (curriculum vitae and references in English language only) demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

•     University degree in Civil engineering;

•     At least 10 years of working experience after attainment of the university degree;

•     At least 7 years of professional experience in similar assignments in the area of supervision and/or works assignments related to adaptation, and/or reconstruction and/or construction of public facilities;

•     Proven experience of the national legislation pertaining to urbanism, design, construction, and supervision, including all the procedures for obtaining construction licenses;

•     Experience for project management/coordination of at least 2 construction projects of above EUR 1.000.000;

•     Experience with FIDIC contracts and/or contract management;

•     Excellent command of spoken and written English language; and

•     Computer skills, including word processing and spreadsheets.
